# Question

**What proportion of people using a public restroom wash their hands?** Harris Interactive, for the American Society for Microbiology (ASM) and the Soap & Detergent Association (SDA), had observers discreetly record the handwashing behaviour of 6,336 adults in public restrooms at six major U.S. attractions (Aug 2005), and separately asked people by telephone whether they *always* wash.

## Data source

Constructed CSV from the published per-venue, per-sex counts (Harris Interactive for ASM/SDA, *A Survey of Hand Washing Behavior — 2005 Findings*). No Lock5 dataset ships for this study. Press headline: 83%; the exact counts give 82.0%.

# Exploratory analysis

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Observed handwashing proportion by venue (dashed line: 91% self-reported rate)"
v = df.groupby("venue", as_index=False)[["n", "washed"]].sum()
v["prop"] = v["washed"] / v["n"]
v = v.sort_values("prop")
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.5, 4.2))
ax.barh(v["venue"], v["prop"], color="#4c72b0")
ax.axvline(0.91, ls="--", color="#c44e52")
ax.text(0.905, 0.1, "self-report 91%", color="#c44e52", ha="right", fontsize=9)
ax.set_xlim(0, 1)
ax.set_xlabel("Observed handwashing proportion")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

# Methods & results

One-proportion inference on p̂ with the Wald interval; parametric z-tests against H₀: p = 0.5 (majority) and H₀: p = 0.91 (self-report), each validated with 100k-replicate randomization and bootstrap.

| Quantity | Value |
|---|---|
| Observed proportion p̂ | **82.0%** (5,195 / 6,336) |
| 95% CI (Wald / bootstrap) | (81.0%, 82.9%) / (81.0%, 82.9%) |
| z vs 50% (majority) | z = 50.9, p < 1e-15 (randomization p < 1e-5) |
| z vs 91% self-report | z = −25.1, p ≈ 8e-139 (randomization p < 1e-5) |
| Female vs male | 89.5% vs 74.6% |

# Decision

**Most people do wash their hands** — but the observed 82% sits dramatically below the 91% self-reported rate. Self-reports of hygiene are inflated by roughly 9 percentage points, and the gap is largest among men (89.5% vs 74.6%). A classic case of social-desirability bias made measurable.
